([[Bradenton, Florida]]) | college = [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]] (2022–2023) | highlights = * [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|AAC Freshman of the Year]] (2023) * Second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2023) * AAC All-Freshman Team (2023) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022]]) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2022) }} '''Jarace Isaiah Walker''' (born September 4, 2003) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] of the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC). He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class. ==High school career== Walker attended [[Susquehannock High School]] in [[York County, Pennsylvania]] for his freshman year before transferring to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].[https://usatodayhss.com/2017/superstar-seventh-grader-jarace-walker-facing-life-changing-decision Superstar seventh-grader Jarace Walker facing life-changing decision][https://www.ydr.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball-boys/2018/02/08/susquehannock-basketball-phenom-taking-his-talents-out-state/318281002/ Susquehannock basketball phenom Jarace Walker taking talents out state][https://www.yorkdispatch.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2020/02/09/york-county-sophomore-jarace-walker-impresses-loss-umbc-event/4708083002/ York County sophomore sensation Jarace Walker impresses despite IMG Academy's loss at UMBC] As a senior, he averaged 16.7 points, 8.2 rebounds and four assists per game. He was selected to play in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022 McDonalds All-American Game]].[https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Jarace-Walker-Houston-Cougars-All-American-team-16804316.php Houston signee Jarace Walker named McDonald's All-American] ===Recruiting=== Walker was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services.
